topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement, framing its significance and acknowledging its notoriously complex nomenclature.

topics.label: Overview of Complement and C3 Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of the complement system, explaining its general logic, naming conventions, and the central role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream pathways that detect pathogens and deposit convertases to reach the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement executes pathogen clearance through opsonization, inflammatory recruitment, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the protective regulatory proteins that prevent complement from destroying healthy host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical manifestations and disease phenotypes associated with deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evade complement attack, focusing on the specialized evasion mechanisms of Staphylococcus aureus and their practical applications.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion of complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
